items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: He went out with Ramsey for a while, then he was out with Wes Montgomery, and he was out with Stanley Turrentine, and Freddie Hubbard, and you know, so this was a time I had all these people.

ctx.x: Somebody take the phone out of your hands—

Yeah. I needed somebody to take the phone, that’s right, that’s right. So it was building and all of a sudden I’m managing ten or twelve people, which is not, doesn’t make sense, because you can not do the job. I learned that quickly, you know, having that many people just wasn’t, didn’t make sense. I had a lot of help, I had different people working with me, but everybody depended on me for the decisions and they wanted to talk to me about anything. items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Les McCann, Ernie Andrews, Randy Crawford, Brook Benton, Ahmad Jamal, Freddie Hubbard

ctx.x: Interviewer: John Mitchell with recording engineer Ken Kimery Institution Description: Transcript, 99 pp.

My name is John Mitchell. I’m a staff writer for the Los Angeles Times. Today is December 10th, 2006. We’re in the home of John Levy and his wife Devra Hall at 1827 Coolidge Avenue, Altadena, California. We’re here as part of the Smithsonian’s Jazz Oral History Project to record John Levy’s story. A former bass player, John has been managing the careers of music artists since 1951. In his musical prime he played the bass when jazz was at its heyday on New York’s 52nd Street.
